ru: отправлять по почте, отправить по почте; высылать, выслать
separable: separable — *mail in the form*, *mail the form in*, and with a pronoun it must split: *mail it in*, never ✗ *mail in it*.
gloss: To send something to an office or a company by mail.
examples: *Mail in* the rebate form within thirty days or you lose it.
She *mailed* her ballot *in* two weeks early.
Half the applications were *mailed in* after the deadline.

separable: fixed — the object is always *it* and nothing else can go there: *they mailed it in*, never ✗ *mailed the concert in*. Informal.
transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object *it*
gloss: To do something with no real effort, just enough to get through it.
examples: The band *mailed it in* for the last three songs.
You can tell he's *mailing it in* until his contract runs out.
They *mail it in* every year against the weaker teams.

ru: брать себя в руки, взять себя в руки; собираться с духом, собраться с духом
separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object at all: *man up and call her*. Informal, and plenty of speakers now find it dated.
gloss: To stop complaining and face something difficult bravely.
examples: *Man up* and tell her the truth.
He finally *manned up* and apologized to the whole team.
She told everybody to *man up* and take the loss.
contrast: *man* doubles its *n* before an ending: *manned up*, *manning up*.

separable: separable — *map out a plan*, *map the whole route out*, *map it out*.
gloss: To plan something in careful detail, step by step.
examples: We *mapped out* the whole trip on a napkin.
She's *mapping out* her first two years of classes.
The strategy was *mapped out* long before the vote.

ru: уценивать, уценить; снижать цену, снизить цену
separable: separable — *mark down the winter coats*, *mark the coats down*, *mark them down*.
gloss: To lower the price of something, usually to sell it faster.
examples: They *marked down* everything in the store after the holidays.
The sofa was *marked down* from nine hundred dollars to five.
They're *marking* the summer stock *down* again this week.

ru: снижать оценку, снизить оценку; снимать баллы
separable: separable — *the teacher marked me down*, *marked down two students*. The reason follows with *for*: *marked down for spelling*.
gloss: To give someone a lower grade or score because of a fault.
examples: That professor *marks* you *down* for every late paper.
I got *marked down* for not citing my sources.
The judges were *marking down* anyone who stepped out of bounds.

separable: separable — *mark off each item*, *mark each item off*, *mark it off*.
gloss: To put a mark beside something on a list to show it is done.
examples: She *marks off* every chore as she finishes it.
He *marked* the last box *off* and went home.
I've *marked off* three of the five apartments we looked at.

ru: повышать цену, повысить цену; делать наценку
separable: separable — *mark up the prices*, *mark the prices up*, *mark them up*.
gloss: To raise the price of something well above what it cost.
examples: The gallery *marks up* every print by three hundred percent.
Restaurants *mark* wine *up* far more than food.
Those jackets have been *marked up* twice since spring.

ru: размечать, разметить; делать пометки, исписать правками
separable: separable — *mark up the draft*, *mark the draft up*, *mark it up*.
gloss: To cover a text or a drawing with corrections and notes.
examples: My editor *marks up* everything I send her.
He *marked* the blueprint *up* before the meeting.
She's *marking up* my essay right now.

separable: separable — *match up the socks*, *match the names up*, *match them up*.
gloss: To put two things together because they belong with each other.
examples: *Match up* each name with a photo.
She *matched* the receipts *up* with the charges on the card.
We're *matching up* mentors and students all week.
contrast: *match* ends in *-ch*, so the third person takes *-es*: *matches up*, never ✗ *matchs up*.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; the other thing follows with *with*: *doesn't match up with the invoice*.
gloss: To agree with or correspond to something else.
examples: His story doesn't *match up* with the security footage.
The totals *matched up* to the penny.
Nothing in the report was *matching up*.

ru: исчерпывать, исчерпать (лимит); доводить до предела, довести до предела
separable: separable when it has an object — *max out the card*, *max the card out*, *max it out*. It is also used with no object: *the server maxed out at noon*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*he maxed out his credit card*), intransitive (*the plan maxes out at five users*)
gloss: To use something all the way up to its limit.
examples: He *maxed out* two credit cards in a single month.
My retirement contribution is already *maxed out* for the year.
The free plan *maxes out* at five users.

separable: separable — *measure out two cups*, *measure the flour out*, *measure it out*.
gloss: To take an exact amount of something out of a larger supply.
examples: *Measure out* three tablespoons of oil.
He *measured out* the dog's food for the whole week.
She was *measuring* the coffee *out* when the phone rang.

ru: соответствовать, оказаться на высоте; дотягивать, дотянуть
separable: nothing to separate — no object; the standard follows with *to*: *measure up to his father*, *measure up to it*.
gloss: To be as good as people expect, or as good as someone else.
examples: The sequel just doesn't *measure up*.
He spent his whole career worrying that he'd never *measure up* to his older brother.
Two of the three finalists *measured up*; the third didn't.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; the subject is the thing that disappears: *her anger melted away*.
gloss: To disappear gradually until there is nothing left.
examples: His nerves *melted away* as soon as he started talking.
The crowd *melted away* after the last song.
Our lead was *melting away* in the fourth quarter.

ru: срываться, сорваться; терять самообладание, потерять самообладание
separable: nothing to separate — in this sense there is no object: *he melted down on live television*. The noun is one word: *a meltdown*.
gloss: To lose emotional control completely.
examples: The toddler *melted down* in the cereal aisle.
He *melts down* every time the wifi drops.
She was *melting down* halfway through the presentation.

separable: nothing to separate — no object: *quit messing around*. (British English says *mess about* for the same thing.)
gloss: To waste time or behave in a silly, unserious way.
examples: Stop *messing around* and finish your homework.
We *messed around* in the parking lot until the doors opened.
He *messes around* all week and then panics on Sunday night.

ru: возиться с, повозиться с; копаться в, лезть в
separable: inseparable — the object follows the whole phrase: *mess around with the settings*, *mess around with them*. ✗ *mess the settings around with*.
gloss: To handle or tinker with something, often without really knowing how it works.
examples: Don't *mess around with* the thermostat.
He *messed around with* the code all afternoon and broke the build.
She's been *messing around with* watercolors since she retired.

separable: nothing to separate — in this sense the verb takes no object at all: *I messed up*, *don't mess up*.
gloss: To make a mistake or do something badly.
examples: I'm sorry — I *messed up*.
He *messes up* whenever the coach is watching.
She was terrified of *messing up* in front of the whole class.
contrast: *mess* ends in *-ss*, so the third person takes *-es*: *messes up*, and the past is *messed up*.

separable: separable — *mess up my plans*, *mess my plans up*, *mess them up*.
gloss: To spoil or ruin something that was going well.
examples: The rain *messed up* our whole weekend.
One bad quarter *messed* the numbers *up* for the year.
Don't *mess* this *up* — we only get one try.

ru: приводить в беспорядок, привести в беспорядок; пачкать, испачкать
separable: separable — *mess up the bed*, *mess the bed up*, *mess it up*.
gloss: To make something dirty or untidy.
examples: The kids *messed up* the living room in five minutes.
The wind *messed* my hair *up* on the way over.
Who's been *messing up* my desk?

ru: связываться с, связаться с; задевать, задеть
separable: inseparable — *don't mess with him*, never ✗ *mess him with*.
gloss: To provoke or challenge someone who can make you regret it.
examples: Nobody *messes with* her older brother.
You picked the wrong guy to *mess with*.
He learned early not to be *messing with* the union.

ru: трогать, тронуть; лезть в, влезть в; портить, испортить
separable: inseparable — the object follows the whole phrase: *someone messed with my settings*, *don't mess with it*.
gloss: To interfere with something you were supposed to leave alone.
examples: Somebody *messed with* my seat adjustment.
Don't *mess with* the wiring unless the power is off.
Who's been *messing with* the file names?

separable: nothing to separate — no object: *a crowd was milling around outside*. (*Mill about* is the same verb.)
gloss: To move about in a crowd with no clear purpose, usually while waiting.
examples: Fans were *milling around* the lobby an hour before the doors opened.
We *milled around* outside until somebody found the key.
A few reporters still *mill around* the courthouse every morning.

ru: упускать, упустить (возможность); оставаться в стороне, остаться в стороне
separable: nothing to separate — no direct object; what you lose follows with *on*: *missed out on the trip*, *missed out on it*. ✗ *missed the trip out*.
gloss: To lose a chance to do or have something good.
examples: Come with us — you'll *miss out* otherwise.
I *missed out* on the early-bird price by one day.
She feels like she's *missing out* on the best years of her kids' lives.

ru: вмешивать, вмешать; подмешивать, подмешать; добавлять, добавить
separable: separable — *mix in the eggs*, *mix the eggs in*, *mix them in*.
gloss: To add an ingredient and stir until it disappears into the rest.
examples: *Mix in* the flour a little at a time.
He *mixed* the berries *in* at the very end.
Once the butter is *mixed in*, the dough comes together fast.

ru: разнообразить, внести разнообразие; менять подход, поменять подход
separable: fixed — the object is always *it*: *let's mix it up*. No other noun can go there in this sense.
transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object *it*
gloss: To change your usual routine so that things stay interesting.
examples: Let's *mix it up* and take the coast road this time.
The coach *mixed it up* in the second half and ran the ball.
She *mixes it up* every week so the class never gets boring.

ru: путать, перепутать; путать местами, перепутать местами
separable: separable — *mix up the twins*, *mix the twins up*, and with a pronoun it must split: *I always mix them up*, never ✗ *mix up them*.
gloss: To mistake one thing or person for another.
examples: I always *mix up* his two sisters.
The pharmacy *mixed* the prescriptions *up*.
Our bags got *mixed up* at the airport.
contrast: *mix* ends in *-x*, so the third person takes *-es*: *mixes up*, never ✗ *mixs up*.

ru: замешивать, замешать; разводить, развести; готовить, приготовить (смесь)
separable: separable — *mix up a batch of batter*, *mix a batch up*. Careful: *mix it up* on its own usually means 'do something differently'.
gloss: To make something by stirring ingredients together.
examples: She *mixed up* a pitcher of lemonade and took it out to the porch.
He's *mixing up* pancake batter.
I *mix up* a big bowl of dressing every Sunday.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; what you fiddle with follows with *with*: *monkeying around with the carburetor*.
gloss: To fool around, or to fiddle with something you should leave alone.
examples: Quit *monkeying around* and get in the car.
He *monkeyed around* with the printer settings and now nothing works.
Those two *monkey around* in the back of the class all period.
contrast: The *-y* here follows a vowel, so it stays: *monkeys around*, *monkeyed around* — never ✗ *monkies*, ✗ *monkied*.

separable: separable — *mop up the spill*, *mop the spill up*, *mop it up*.
gloss: To soak up spilled liquid with a cloth or a mop.
examples: He *mopped up* the milk before it reached the rug.
*Mop* that *up* before somebody slips.
She's still *mopping up* after the pipe burst.

separable: separable — *mop up the last few claims*, *mop them up*.
gloss: To finish off the last small part of a job or a fight.
examples: Two of us stayed late to *mop up* the last of the paperwork.
Their closer *mopped up* the ninth inning in eleven pitches.
Troops spent another week *mopping up* pockets of resistance.

separable: nothing to separate — no object, though a place can follow *around*: *moped around the house all day*.
gloss: To go about looking sad and doing nothing, feeling sorry for yourself.
examples: He *moped around* the house for a week after the breakup.
Stop *moping around* and call her.
She *mopes around* every Sunday night before work.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; the subject is the thing piling up: *the bills mounted up*.
gloss: To grow larger and larger bit by bit, usually about costs or problems.
examples: Small charges *mount up* fast on that card.
The medical bills *mounted up* while he was out of work.
Complaints have been *mounting up* since the redesign.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; the person takes *to* and the subject takes *about*: *mouthed off to the ref about a call*.
gloss: To talk back rudely and disrespectfully.
examples: He got benched for *mouthing off* to the coach.
Don't *mouth off* to your mother.
She *mouthed off* one time too many and lost the job.

separable: nothing to separate — no object: *move along, folks*.
gloss: To keep going instead of stopping, or to keep making steady progress.
examples: The officer told the crowd to *move along*.
The line *moved along* faster than I expected.
Things are *moving along* nicely on the remodel.

ru: переезжать с места на место, часто переезжать
separable: nothing to separate — no object: *we moved around a lot*.
gloss: To change where you live again and again.
examples: We *moved around* a lot when I was a kid — six schools in nine years.
Army families *move around* every couple of years.
After college he kept *moving around* until he landed in Denver.

ru: переезжать, переехать (в другой город); уезжать, уехать
separable: nothing to separate — no object; the place you leave takes *from*: *moved away from Cleveland*.
gloss: To leave the town where you live and go live somewhere else.
examples: My best friend *moved away* in third grade.
They're *moving away* as soon as the house sells.
Half my class has *moved away* since graduation.

separable: nothing to separate — no object: *moved back to Texas*, *moved back in with her parents*.
gloss: To return to live in a place where you used to live.
examples: After the divorce she *moved back* to Ohio.
He's *moving back* in with his parents to save money.
They *moved back* two years after leaving.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; the plan follows with *with*: *move forward with the merger*.
gloss: To go ahead with a plan instead of waiting or stopping.
examples: The board voted to *move forward* with the merger.
We *moved forward* without waiting for legal.
Nothing is *moving forward* until the funding clears.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; the place takes *to* or *into* and a person takes *with*: *moved in with her sister*.
gloss: To start living in a new home.
examples: We *moved in* on the first of the month.
New neighbors are *moving in* downstairs.
She *moved in* with her boyfriend last spring.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; to name the target add *on*: *moved in on the building*.
gloss: To come steadily closer, especially in order to attack or take control.
examples: SWAT *moved in* at four in the morning.
A storm is *moving in* from the west.
Federal agents *move in* only once the warrants are signed.

ru: подступать к, подступить к; посягать на, посягнуть на
separable: inseparable — the object follows the whole phrase: *moved in on the suspect*, *moved in on him*. ✗ *moved him in on*.
gloss: To close in on someone or something in order to seize or attack it.
examples: Police *moved in on* the house just before dawn.
A national chain is *moving in on* their customers.
They *move in on* a company the minute its stock slips.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; what comes next follows with *to*: *move on to the next slide*.
gloss: To leave one subject or task and start the next one.
examples: Any questions? If not, let's *move on*.
We *moved on* to the budget after twenty minutes.
He kept *moving on* before anyone could answer.

ru: забывать, забыть (прошлое); начинать новую жизнь, начать новую жизнь
separable: nothing to separate — no object; what you leave behind takes *from*: *move on from a breakup*.
gloss: To stop being upset about something in the past and get on with your life.
examples: It took her a year to *move on*.
He's *moved on* — he's seeing somebody new.
You can't keep rereading his emails; you have to start *moving on*.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; the place follows with *of*: *moved out of the apartment*.
gloss: To stop living in a place and take your things with you.
examples: He *moved out* the day the lease ended.
They're *moving out* at the end of the semester.
She's *moved out* twice and come back both times.

ru: подвигаться, подвинуться; освобождать место, освободить место
separable: nothing to separate — no object: *move over*, *could you move over a little?*
gloss: To shift sideways so that someone else has room.
examples: *Move over* — there's room for one more.
He *moved over* so she could see the screen.
Everybody *moved over* one seat.

separable: separable when it has an object — *they moved her up to manager*, *moved him up*. Most often there is no object at all: *she moved up fast*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*he moved up quickly*), transitive (*they moved her up a level*)
gloss: To rise to a higher position, rank, or level.
examples: She *moved up* from intern to director in four years.
They *moved* him *up* to the varsity team.
Nobody in that department is *moving up*.

ru: переносить на более ранний срок, перенести на более ранний срок
separable: separable — *move up the meeting*, *move the meeting up*, *move it up*.
gloss: To reschedule something for an earlier time or date.
examples: Can we *move* the meeting *up* to nine?
They *moved up* the launch by two weeks.
The wedding is being *moved up* because of his deployment.

separable: separable — *mowed down two cyclists*, *mowed them down*.
gloss: To knock down or kill people in numbers, with a vehicle or with gunfire.
examples: A drunk driver *mowed down* two cyclists on the shoulder.
The guns *mowed* them *down* as they crossed the field.
He's been *mowing down* hitters all season.
contrast: In this phrasal verb American English keeps the regular past participle: *mowed down*, not ✗ *mown down* (*mown* survives only as an adjective: *newly mown grass*).

separable: never split — usually there is no object at all (*we muddled through*), and when *through* takes one it follows the whole phrase: *muddled through the interview*. ✗ *muddled the interview through*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*we muddled through*), transitive (*she muddled through the speech*)
gloss: To get to the end of something badly but somehow, without really knowing what you are doing.
examples: Neither of us reads music, so we just *muddled through*.
She *muddled through* the interview in her broken Spanish.
They're *muddling through* until the new director starts.

separable: separable — *mull over the offer*, *mull the offer over*, and with a pronoun it must split: *let me mull it over*, never ✗ *mull over it*.
gloss: To think about something slowly and carefully before deciding.
examples: Let me *mull it over* and call you tomorrow.
She *mulled over* the job offer for a solid week.
He's still *mulling over* whether to sell the house.
contrast: *mull* already ends in a double *l*, so nothing is added: *mulled over*, *mulling over*.

separable: nothing to separate — no object; what you force your way into follows with *on*: *muscled in on our territory*.
gloss: To force your way into something so as to take a share of what other people have.
examples: A national chain is *muscling in* on the local market.
He *muscled in* on a deal two other firms had spent a year building.
Nobody *muscles in* on that neighborhood.

separable: separable, but in practice the object follows the particle — *muster up the courage*, *muster up enough support*. A pronoun can split it: *he finally mustered it up*.
gloss: To gather enough of a feeling or a quality to do something hard.
examples: It took him a month to *muster up* the nerve to ask.
She *mustered up* a smile and shook his hand.
They couldn't *muster up* enough votes to pass it.
